newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portuguese shares hit new highs, banks lead way.
newsitem.headline: Portuguese shares hit new highs, banks lead way.

text.p: Shares surged to take the PSI20 to a new peak, with banks leading the way.

*Banco Comercial Portugues jumped 3.7 percent to close at 3,244 escudos after hitting a record high of 3,280 during the session. Banco Sotto Mayor was also up some 2.5 percent, with Banco Portugues de Investimento gaining over two percent.
*Dealers said that providing international markets and the dollar remained strong, the stock market could gain further.
*"We are pretty dependent on what happens elsewhere," said one trader.

*Others noted that the selling noted in past sessions to make room in portfolios for the soon-to-be-privatised EDP electricity company was coming to an end with investors realising demand was going to be very heavy and the allotment low.
*Although it closed just four escudos up at 1,563 escudos, engineering group Efacec was once again the focus of very heavy trade of nearly 450,000 shares.

*According to market sources, the heavy business of recent sessions is due to the entry of a new institutional shareholder, linked to the BPI group. Efacec issued a statement, however, on the brokers' Tradis trading system saying it was not aware of any institutional interest.
*Jeronimo Martins rocketed just over six percent but traders could provide no explanation. Turnover, however, was modest.
*Business in paper group Inapa was just a passage of stock within the Banco Espirito Santo group.
